summary:
Earth System Trend Detective is an interactive web application that helps students and the public explore how our planet is changing using NASA data. Users can select an environmental variable and region to see how it has changed over time.
Our project uses NASA POWER data, based on MERRA-2 reanalysis and GPM satellite observations, to study monthly air temperature and rainfall from 2001 to 2024 across eight regions, including Kerala, Rajasthan, Assam and the Central Amazon.
The application calculates Sen's Slope to measure the rate of change and uses the Mann-Kendall test to determine whether a trend is statistically significant. We also apply False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction to improve reliability when comparing multiple regions.
Results are displayed through interactive maps, graphs and simple explanations. Users can see whether a variable is increasing, decreasing or showing no clear trend.
The same environmental variable may increase in one region and decrease in another. Even when a trend is not statistically significant, it is worth monitoring because changes may become important over time.
Our goal is to make NASA Earth science data easier to understand and help people explore environmental changes around them.
details:
EarthTrend Dashboard – Be an Earth System Trend Detective!

1. What does our project do?

EarthTrend Dashboard is an interactive, student-friendly website designed to help users understand how Earth's environment changes over time. It allows users to explore historical environmental data, select geographical locations, compare different years, and identify increasing or decreasing environmental trends.

Our main aim is to make complex Earth observation data easier to understand through visual representations such as charts, graphs, and maps.

2. How does it work?

Users can visit our website, select a geographical location, choose an available time period, and explore environmental information. The website presents the available data through visualisations, helping users compare different years and observe environmental patterns.

We use NASA's GIOVANNI platform as a source for collecting Earth observation datasets. These datasets help us explore environmental changes over time.

3. What are its benefits?

  • Makes complex environmental data easier to understand.
  • Helps students explore real-world environmental information.
  • Encourages data analysis and scientific thinking.
  • Helps users identify environmental patterns and changes.
  • Creates awareness about Earth's changing systems.
  • Makes environmental learning more interactive.

4. Intended impact

Our project aims to make Earth science more accessible to students and young learners. It encourages students to explore scientific data, understand environmental changes, and develop curiosity about our planet. It can be useful for educational activities, classroom learning, science projects, and environmental awareness.

5. Tools and technologies used

  • NASA GIOVANNI – Environmental data collection.
  • Python – Data processing and analysis.
  • Visualisation tools – To present environmental information through charts and graphs.
  • Vercel – Website hosting and deployment.

6. What makes our project creative?

Our project connects NASA Earth observation data with student-friendly interactive learning. Instead of presenting environmental information only as numbers, we aim to make it easier to explore and compare through visualisations.

EarthTrend Dashboard transforms environmental data exploration into an engaging learning experience.

Our Vision: Explore the past, understand the present, and discover how our Earth is changing.
